theorem.input: Graph C with exact lists L(v) subseteq [4] and a two-vertex separator S={u,v} such that C-S has connected components Q1,...,Qt with t>=2.
theorem.separator_state_space: Col_L(C[S]) = all proper list-respecting colorings sigma:S->[4]. Because |S|=2 and palette=[4], |Col_L(C[S])|<=4^2=16.
theorem.boundary_lists: For sigma in Col_L(C[S]), define L_i^sigma(x)=L(x) minus the colors sigma(s) of all separator vertices s in S adjacent to x.
theorem.equivalence: C is list-colorable iff there exists sigma in Col_L(C[S]) such that every (Qi,L_i^sigma) is list-colorable.

proof.forward: Restrict any proper list-coloring of C to S and to each component Qi. The restriction sigma is proper and list-respecting on C[S]; every neighbor x of s must avoid sigma(s), so the component restrictions respect L_i^sigma.
proof.reverse: Choose one proper list-respecting separator state sigma and independently color every component Qi from L_i^sigma. Distinct components of C-S have no edges between them, and every edge from a component to S is already enforced by the restricted lists, so the colorings glue with sigma to a proper list-coloring of C.

theorem.reconstruction: Union all independently reconstructed Qi colorings with the fixed boundary assignment sigma.
theorem.UNSAT_logic: C is uncolorable iff every sigma in Col_L(C[S]) is rejected because at least one downstream component is uncolorable.
theorem.complexity_overhead: At most 16 boundary states, plus polynomial propagation/component decomposition and the sum of authorized downstream component solvers.

proof_carrying_certificate.separator: Verify |S|=2 and C-S has at least two connected components.
proof_carrying_certificate.component_partition: Verify the Qi partition V(C)\S and no original edge joins different Qi.
proof_carrying_certificate.state_validity: Verify each enumerated sigma is proper on C[S] and respects both exact lists.
proof_carrying_certificate.per_state: Preserve exact boundary-restricted/propagated lists and downstream terminal certificates.
proof_carrying_certificate.aggregation: A sigma branch is SAT iff all components are SAT; global SAT is existential over sigma.

distinctions.not_backdoor: This is exact graph-separator factorization. It does not assert that choosing two arbitrary vertices destroys complexity inside one coupled component.
distinctions.no_treewidth_claim: The theorem does not require bounded treewidth of C.

source_alignment.Paper_II: The source framework explicitly treats separating connected components into different instances as a normal-subcase simplification; this theorem is a separate exact list-coloring composition fact, not a theorem claimed by Paper II.
